scope: Reviewed OMAI formula endpoints and exact Lean proof source for local theorems with no Physlib physics counterpart. Hash and compiled-name checks detect drift and provenance errors; they are not automatic symbolic translation or numerical validation.

operators.formula_latex: \kappa_{c} = \frac{k_{m} \left(2 f_{vol} \left(- k_{m} + \left(1 - \frac{k_{m}}{G_{int} a_{rad}}\right) {k_{f}}_{3,3}\right) + 2 k_{m} + \left(1 + \frac{2 k_{m}}{G_{int} a_{rad}}\right) {k_{f}}_{3,3}\right)}{- f_{vol} \left(- k_{m} + \left(1 - \frac{k_{m}}{G_{int} a_{rad}}\right) {k_{f}}_{3,3}\right) + 2 k_{m} + \left(1 + \frac{2 k_{m}}{G_{int} a_{rad}}\right) {k_{f}}_{3,3}}

interpretations: DepolarizationFactor carries the polar factor L33 of an axially symmetric spheroid with symmetry axis 3 and aspect ratio p = d3/d1 > 0 (p > 1 prolate, p < 1 oblate); L11 = (1 - L33)/2 is the catalog's auxiliary sum rule and is not proved.

The Nan formulas read the matrix conductivity k_m, the filler conductivities k_f[1,1] (transverse to axis 3) and k_f[3,3] (along axis 3), the full particle dimensions d_1 and d_3, the interface conductance G_int, the filler volume fraction f_vol in [0, 1] and the depolarization factors, in the catalog's input order. The per-direction interface-corrected filler conductivity k / (1 + 2 k / (G_int d)) is the convention of Nan, Liu, Lin and Li, Appl. Phys. Lett. 85, 3549 (2004); away from p = 1 it is a slab approximation.

G_int = q_int / Delta T_int > 0 with Delta T_int the temperature drop in the direction of the heat flux; the factor 2 counts the two interfaces a particle presents along a direction, and one G_int applies to every face.

Random means isotropic three-dimensional orientation. The aligned operator is the component along the alignment axis 3, which is the through-plane direction only for platelets; the transverse companion is an auxiliary formula and is not proved.

The Hasselman-Johnson formula reads k_m, the filler k_f[3,3] (the sphere conductivity), the sphere radius a_rad, G_int and f_vol. The catalog's d is a diameter, so the two formulas agree for spheres with d_1 = d_3 = 2 a_rad, L11 = L33 = 1/3 and k_f[1,1] = k_f[3,3]; inserting the radius into d doubles the interface penalty.

f_vol is a volume fraction, not a mass fraction or a percentage. Particles are monodisperse. All conductivities, G_int and lengths are positive and in one coherent unit system; the theorems are dilute effective-medium identities and bounds, not statements about percolating or strongly interacting fillers.
